strongest_argument: The claim is not a discovery, it is a summary of two press releases. Qfin's 'external funding costs rose about 25 basis points during July and August' is in its GlobeNewswire results release of 2026-08-25, and FinVolution's China volume being 'down around 50% in July' plus a 30bp Q3 funding-cost rise is in its GlobeNewswire release and call of 2026-08-27, transcribed the same day by Investing.com under the headline 'profit rises as China funding tightens', and by Seeking Alpha, the Globe and Mail, Yahoo and Bamboo Works. The claimant's own wording concedes it: FinVolution 'told investors' and Qifu 'said'. Every LX holder reads the two closest comparables' earnings calls, and the tape shows they did - LX fell 11.28% over the five sessions ending 2026-08-28, precisely the window containing XYF (08-24), QFIN (08-25/26) and FINV (08-27), leaving it 2.16% off its 52-week low and 65% down over twelve months against FinVolution's 32%. That dispersion is the market already discriminating between these names and assigning LX the worst outcome, which is exactly what the claimant says it has not done. The wider thesis fares no better: LX's RMB57.9bn originations, +15.9% QoQ, come from LX's own release of 2026-05-25 and have been public for three months, alongside management's guidance that Q2 originations would be flat, and a cross-sectional lender comparison naming Lexin, QFIN, FINV and XYF was published on 2026-07-21. Note also the timing: a July volume collapse and July-August funding costs are Q3 events and cannot be in the June quarter LX reports on 08-31.

prior_publication.what_it_says: Qfin's Q2 results release and call, management stating external funding costs rose about 25bp during July and August and may keep trending higher in H2.
FinVolution's Q2 release, with the call disclosing that an industry credit event caused China volume to fall roughly 50% in July and funding costs to rise 30bp in Q3.
Same-day wire transcript headlined on the China funding tightening - the exact fact the claim treats as unpublished.
LX's own Q1 release giving RMB57.9bn originations, +15.9% QoQ - the premise of the wider thesis, public for three months, with guidance that Q2 originations would be flat.
Published cross-sectional review of the Chinese loan facilitators with per-name origination trajectories under the 24% cap - the peer read-through as a standing exercise, not a discovery.
Caixin on the NFRA/PBOC crackdown forcing down all-in borrowing costs, with the disclosure rule effective 1 August - the structural backdrop, covered for five months.
LX-specific coverage of a 16.5% decline attributing it to Chinese consumer credit and regulatory concerns and explicitly to rising funding costs.
X Financial's Q2 call, the third peer print inside LX's five-day drawdown window, describing deliberate volume contraction under the 24% cap.

baseline_evidence: LX spot $1.18; run_up_5d -11.28% and run_up_20d -19.18%; 81.33% below the 52-week high and only 2.16% above the 52-week low. The five-day window ending 2026-08-28 brackets XYF (08-24), QFIN (08-25/26) and FINV (08-27) - the stock lost 11.3% while those disclosures were being made, which is the read-through executing in the tape rather than waiting for the print. Relative dispersion confirms discrimination: LX -65% over twelve months against FinVolution -32%. Options are unusable (no two-sided ATM legs, no skew, put/call OI 0.37 on 3,189 contracts), so the cash move carries the argument.
materiality: material, but against Q3 rather than the quarter being reported. A ~50% July volume drop and 25-30bp of funding cost sit outside LX's June quarter entirely, so they bear on guidance rather than the printed P&L; the absent provision-release cushion is material against RMB201m quarterly net income, and that risk is already reflected in a share price 81% off its high.
what_would_change_my_verdict: Evidence that LX rallied or held flat through 2026-08-24 to 08-28 while peers reported, or a specific LX quantification - its Q2 provision coverage or reserve build against the RMB57.9bn book - that no published source has computed and that the -11.28% peer-week move cannot plausibly have discounted.
